ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, in $\triangle ABC$, $\angle A=40^\circ$, $AB=AC$, and the perpendicular bisector $MN$ of $AB$ intersects $AC$ at point D and $AB$ at point E. The perimeter of $\triangle ABC$ is $13cm$, $AB=5cm$. What is the degree measure of $\angle DBC$?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} \\
Since $AB=AC$, \\
it follows that $\triangle ABC$ is an isosceles triangle, \\
because $\angle A=40^\circ$, \\
thus $\angle ABC=\angle ACB=\frac{1}{2}\left(180^\circ-40^\circ\right)=70^\circ$, \\
since $MN$ is the perpendicular bisector of $AB$, \\
it follows that $\triangle ABD$ is an isosceles triangle, \\
therefore $\angle ABD=\angle A=40^\circ$, \\
hence $\angle DBC=\angle ABC-\angle ABD=70^\circ-40^\circ=\boxed{30^\circ}$;
